themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints in Bed-Stuy spiked to 73 THIS WEEK, a 297% jump from the 8-week baseline average of 18.4 weekly complaints (z-score: 4.76), suggesting a sudden infrastructure failure or pothole epidemic affecting multiple blocks.
evidence: 73 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 18.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (297% increase, z-score 4.76)
Spike appears localized to single week, suggesting acute event or cluster rather than gradual deterioration
Represents largest volume spike across all 311 categories monitored this week
reporting_angles: Map the 73 complaints to identify geographic hotspot(s)—is this concentrated on one avenue or scattered across the district?
Interview DOT about what triggered the spike and timeline for repairs; compare response time to other NYC districts
Talk to residents about safety risks (ankle injuries, vehicle damage) and how long streets have been in this condition

themes_detail.label: Public Drinking & Disorderly Conduct Surge
themes_detail.summary: Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints jumped 357% to 16 THIS WEEK (vs. 3.5 weekly average) and public drinking complaints hit 3 THIS WEEK (vs. 0.2 average)—a combined 1100% spike—signaling a potential public order deterioration or enforcement change in real-time.
evidence: Drinking complaints: 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% increase, z-score 6.35)
Non-Emergency Police Matters: 16 THIS WEEK vs. 3.5 weekly average (357% increase, z-score 5.0)
Both spikes occurred in the same week, suggesting correlated public disorder event or enforcement initiative
reporting_angles: Obtain NYPD weekly enforcement logs for CD 303 to determine if increased police activity or arrests drove the spike
Interview precinct commander and community board about whether new enforcement strategy or hotspot emerged this week
Visit key complaint locations and interview business owners, residents about visibility of drinking/disorder and safety concerns

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Deterioration Spike
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints surged to 17 LAST WEEK, a 189% increase from the 5.9 weekly average (z-score: 5.33), indicating emerging pedestrian hazards across the district that may overlap with the street condition crisis.
evidence: 17 sidewalk condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 5.9 weekly average (189% increase, z-score 5.33)
Spike predates this week's street condition explosion by one week, suggesting condition deterioration may be accelerating
Combined with street spike, points to systemic infrastructure failure across pedestrian/vehicle surfaces
reporting_angles: Cross-reference sidewalk complaints with street complaints to identify overlapping neighborhoods and block-by-block conditions
Interview DOE about impact on school routes and student safety; check if any schools issued alerts about hazardous conditions
Photograph worst-affected sidewalks and quantify trip/fall hazards; determine if elderly or disabled residents have reported injuries

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary Conditions & Animal Issues
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary animal complaints on private property spiked 700% to 4 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO (vs. 0.5 weekly average, z-score: 7.0), and broader dirty condition complaints hit 109 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO (198% spike)—a sustained sanitation crisis potentially linked to pest or waste management failures.
evidence: Unsanitary animal private property: 4 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (700% increase, z-score 7.0—highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
Dirty condition complaints: 109 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 36.6 weekly average (198% increase, z-score 5.49)
Two correlated spikes suggest systemic sanitation failure, possibly rodent/pest infestation or waste collection breakdown
reporting_angles: File FOIL request for DOHMH pest inspection records in CD 303 over past 4 weeks to determine if rodent/animal issues triggered response
Interview Sanitation about waste collection changes, labor shortages, or missed pickups in the district during this 3-week window
Document affected properties and interview residents about visible pests, odors, and how long conditions have persisted since spike

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Accumulation
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints jumped 700% to 6 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO (vs. 0.8 weekly average, z-score: 6.33), suggesting rapid accumulation of debris on streets that may signal either dockless bike program failure or inadequate city enforcement.
evidence: 6 abandoned bike complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.8 weekly average (700% increase, z-score 6.33)
Spike appears isolated to 2-week window, not sustained, but statistically significant
Aligns with broader street/sidewalk deterioration theme suggesting general infrastructure neglect
reporting_angles: Map the 6 complaint locations to identify if bikes are concentrated near transit hubs, parks, or specific neighborhoods
Interview Citi Bike and dockless operators (Jump, Lime) about complaints and enforcement response in Bed-Stuy during this 2-week window
Check if DOT has removal data and determine lag time between complaint and bike removal
